dosing.evidence: Freshly dissolved into saline to achieve the desired concentrations [high dose (0.3), middle dose (0.03), low dose (0.015 mg/kg)] of (R)-DOI hydrochloride...were given as 0.1 mL subcutaneous (sc) injections.

day_night_flipped.evidence: All mice were maintained on a 12:12 light-dark cycle (lights on at 6 a.m. and off at 6 p.m.). All behavioral experiments were done during the animals' active phase (scotophase).

judge_notes: Merged candidate gptoss's four separate SAM assay entries (Escape proportion, Latency, Socially induced freezing, Attention to escape route) into a single SAM assay — these are all distinct behavioural measures collected within the same 5-min SAM apparatus session, so they count as one assay with multiple measures.
Kept Home Cage Locomotion and Fear Conditioning Test (Day 5 in SAM without aggressor) as separate assays because they are distinct paradigms with different apparatus contexts/protocols.

Housing group_housing: scored 'no' because the paper explicitly states mice were separated into individual cages prior to behavioral experiments, though they were group-housed during the 5-day acclimation period.
SAM B5/E7: scored as Free social interaction / Free social group because the focal mouse and CD1 aggressor freely interact in the open field without barriers.
SAM E1: scored Standard apparatus (rather than Enriched arena) — the SAM is a standard rectangular box with two divider-formed compartments; this is apparatus architecture, not enrichment.

SAM E2 shelter: although safety areas exist behind dividers, only the small escape tunnel apex allows the test mouse to leave the open field — scored 0 conservatively, consistent with gptoss; the safety zones are part of the apparatus design rather than refuges available to all mice during recording.
B7 scored 0 for all assays: ANYmaze is position-tracking software per rubric SCORE-0 list.
Fear Conditioning Test time_to_assay: ~3 days after last dose (Day 2 injection, Day 5 test) → short_term_1to7d.

assays.assay_description: Test C57BL/6N mice exposed to a novel aggressive CD1 mouse in a rectangular box (91 × 22 × 30 cm) with two safety areas behind curved dividers, each with a small apical escape tunnel. Each daily session is 5 min over 4 consecutive days, preceded by a tone-cued fear conditioning element. Behaviours measured: latency to escape, % escaping, socially induced freezing, attention to escape route (time within 3 cm of escape hole), jumps. Drug administered after Day 2; behavioural changes assessed on Days 3 and 4 across (R)-DOI doses (0.015, 0.03, 0.3 mg/kg) vs. vehicle.

application_type.evidence: were given as 0.1 mL subcutaneous (sc) injections

setup_habituation.evidence: Paper does not describe pre-test apparatus habituation for SAM.

setup_restrain.evidence: Test mice are placed in an opaque cylinder...the cylinder is lifted, exposing each test mouse a novel aggressive CD1 mouse in the SAM open field for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food was placed in the SAM arena during the 5-min test; home cage had ad libitum food.

water_restriction.evidence: No water was placed in the SAM arena during the 5-min test; home cage had ad libitum water.

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately following SAM social interactions on Day 2, mice were given sc injections...Days 3 and 4 of the SAM to determine how psychedelic treatment impacts stress coping strategies

sample_size.evidence: vehicle-treated animals (N = 28) and (R)-DOI treatment (3 dosages: 0.015 mg/kg, N = 20; 0.03 mg/kg, N = 17; 0.3 mg/kg, N = 25). Escape middle dose N=7.

outcomes.summary: Single sc (R)-DOI shifted Stay (stress-vulnerable) mice toward active coping: low (0.015 mg/kg) and middle (0.03 mg/kg) doses increased the proportion escaping, reduced latency to escape, increased attention to the escape route, and reduced socially induced freezing on Days 3 and 4. The high dose (0.3 mg/kg) was least effective on coping but reduced freezing in Escape mice on Day 3. Effects were dose-dependent and not monotonic with the lowest doses most efficacious.
outcomes.statistics: Escape proportion (Stay, low dose Day 3): χ²: F1 = 2.8, p ≤ 0.029; Day 4 middle and low doses: χ²: F1 = 4.3, p ≤ 0.039. Latency (Stay): middle t20 = 2.1, p ≤ 0.05; low t20 = 2.6, p ≤ 0.019 on Day 3; Escape low Day 4 t20 = 2.4, p ≤ 0.024. Freezing (Stay Day 4): F3,39 = 3.1, p ≤ 0.037; middle dose t20 = 2.6, p ≤ 0.018. Attention (Stay): F3,38 = 4.2, p ≤ 0.011 Day 3; low dose Day 3 t19 = 2.7, p ≤ 0.016; Day 4 t20 = 3.7, p < 0.001.
outcomes.evidence: Stay mice treated with the lowest dose (0.015 mg/kg) of (R)-DOI had a significantly higher proportion of animals that escaped on Day 3 compared to vehicle-treated Stay animals (40% increase; χ2: F1 = 2.8, p ≤ 0.029).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Behaviors that were recorded include latency to escape, contextual and cued freezing, socially induced freezing, attention to the escape route, and number of jumps.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Outcomes reported as single totals/averages per 5-min session; between-day comparisons are not within-session temporal dynamics.

B4_ethological.evidence: Social interaction with a live CD1 aggressor, including socially induced freezing and active escape investigation, is from the species' natural repertoire.

B5_social.evidence: exposing each test mouse a novel aggressive CD1 mouse (unconditioned stimulus, US) in the SAM open field for 5 min

B6_cognitive.evidence: fear conditioning is the initial step that begins each day of the SAM...the time it takes an animal to escape declines over the 4-day paradigm, suggesting that spatial and/or social learning is occurring

B7_automated_classification.evidence: videos were stored for later behavioral analysis using ANYmaze Video Tracking Software (Version 6.0, Stoelting Co, Wood Dale, IL) or scored manually

B8_multivariate.evidence: Univariate ANOVAs and t-tests reported; no PCA/clustering.

outcomes.summary: Home-cage locomotion was slightly elevated in mice that received the lowest (0.015 mg/kg) (R)-DOI dose compared with all other groups; higher doses did not change locomotion.
outcomes.evidence: Locomotion in the home cage following (R)-DOI treatment was slightly elevated in the lowest (0.015 mg/kg) dose compared to all other groups (Fig. S3); but was not affected by higher dosages.

assays.assay_description: On Day 5, mice tested for tone-cued and contextual freezing in the SAM apparatus without the CD1 aggressor (no US), to assess fear conditioning developed across Days 1-4.

time_to_assay.evidence: On Day 5, C57BL/6N mice are tested for fear conditioning (FC) responses (freezing) in the SAM without the unconditioned stimulus. Drug given after Day 2 (~3 days prior).

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes for Day 5 fear-conditioning test reported in Fig. S4 (supplementary).

outcomes.summary: Fear-conditioned freezing on Day 5 was not affected by (R)-DOI in Stay mice (cued > contextual at all doses, as in vehicle). In Escape mice, (R)-DOI at all doses prevented the typical enhancement of cued freezing relative to contextual.
outcomes.evidence: freezing induced by fear conditioning was not affected by DOI (Fig. S4)...However, (R)-DOI treatment, at all doses, in Escape mice prevented enhanced freezing during cued conditioning (Fig. S4C).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Pre-tone vs. post-tone freezing analyses parse within-session time-course around the CS.
